intended_object: The canonical real embedding X → X_ℂ = X ⊕ iX, x ↦ x + i·0, of a real vector space into its complexification. Taken from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation: The library defines `Complexification X` as a structure of pairs (re, im). `ofReal x := ⟨x, 0⟩` sends x to the element with real part x and imaginary part 0, which is exactly x + i·0. The only assumption is `[Zero X]`, the least needed to write down the zero imaginary part, so the definition is not too narrow. The library then proves the properties expected of this map: its real and imaginary parts (`ofReal_re`, `ofReal_im`), that it is an isometry (`norm_ofReal`), and that complex-linear maps out of X_ℂ are determined by their values on its image (`ext_ofReal`). Mathlib has no general complexification of a real vector space in this form, so there is no direct counterpart.
